name: Roman-Inspired Mixed-Green Salad (Misticanza alla Romana)

ingredients.name: wild leafy greens and tender fresh herbs

instructions.primary_message: Pick over the leafy vegetables, discarding any wilted or damaged leaves. Cut lettuce leaves free of their cores, pick tender herbs from stems, and quarter, core, and slice tight leafy heads like radicchio and endive. Wash everything in several changes of water until no dirt or grit remains. Dry well in a salad spinner.
In large serving bowl, gently toss salad with just enough olive oil to gently coat leaves. Add splash of lemon juice and salt to taste, tossing to combine. Serve.

schema_metadata.keywords: chicory, green, herb, Italian, lettuce, Roman, salad

description: For a truly great mixed greens salad, make your own mix with the freshest stuff you can find: whole heads of lettuce, radicchio, herbs, dandelion greens, and more.
notes:
Optional substitutions: wild leafy greens and tender fresh herbs → cultivated leafy greens and tender fresh herbs; Kosher salt → sea salt

Notes: The key here is to use what you can get, and not try to force anything into the salad that won't be great. If you live near a farm stand or farmers market, that may be your best bet.If not, or if it's not the right season, stick to hardy leafy vegetables and herbs like radicchio, endive, romaine, escarole, frisée, and baby kale.
author: Daniel Gritzer
